USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

Mucus regulation rather than immediate bronchodilation

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

In a study of irritant-exposed airways, a cysteine-derived oral drug changes the composition of secreted mucus glycoproteins and reduces goblet-cell hyperplasia. It does not produce an immediate rise in airflow through smooth-muscle relaxation. Which description best fits carbocisteine?

  1. A mucus-regulating mucolytic
  2. A short-acting beta2 agonist
  3. A competitive muscarinic antagonist
  4. An extracellular DNA-cleaving enzyme
  5. A central opioid antitussive
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

A mucus-regulating mucolytic

Carbocisteine modifies abnormal mucus properties; it is not an acute bronchodilator.

Understanding the options

A mucus-regulating mucolytic
Changes in mucus glycoproteins and goblet cells fit carbocisteine.
A short-acting beta2 agonist
Beta2 agonists primarily relax airway smooth muscle.
A competitive muscarinic antagonist
Muscarinic antagonists block cholinergic airway signaling rather than this described mucus regulation.
An extracellular DNA-cleaving enzyme
DNA cleavage describes dornase alfa.
A central opioid antitussive
Central opioid action suppresses cough rather than regulating mucus glycoproteins.
